- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates reversal; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance or add 0.5–1.5% buffer for volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts prices above 3–5-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates tail risk in bullish sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment > 0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a bottom too early; delay forecast by 1–2 days or reduce magnitude by 1–2% to avoid premature reversal.
